s.g: (slang, often in the plural) A knuckle duster.
(archaic, slang) A thief or pickpocket.
Any of the joints between the bones of the fingers.
(by extension) A mechanical joint.
(sports, billiards, snooker, pool) The curved part of the cushion at the entrance to the pockets on a cue sports table.
The kneejoint of a quadruped, especially of a calf; formerly, the kneejoint of a human being.
A cut of meat of various kinds.
s.x: Beef knuckle is from the knee joint. Pork knuckle, or ham hock, is from the joint between the tibia/fibula and the metatarsals of the foot of a pig, where the foot was attached to the leg.

s.g: (transitive) To apply pressure, or rub or massage with one's knuckles (noun sense 1).
s.x: He knuckled the sleep from his eyes.

s.g: (transitive, slang) To strike or punch.
(intransitive) To bend the fingers.
(intransitive) To touch one's forehead as a mark of respect.
(intransitive, figurative) To yield.
(baseball) A pitch thrown with the ball gripped on the fingertips and released with no rotation, which travels over an unpredictable path to the plate due to microturbulence in the air.
s.x: Even the pitcher doesn't know where his knuckleball is going.

s.g: (cricket) A type of delivery where a fast bowler holds the ball on the knuckles of the index and middle fingers.
(figurative, informal) An event that is hard to predict.
s.x: Our vendor keeps throwing us knuckleballs.

s.g: (intransitive, baseball) To pitch knuckleballs.

Such a bone once used in knucklebones and other children's games of chance.
(slang) A die.
A children's game, originally played with the knucklebones of sheep, in which small objects are picked up, moved, thrown, and caught according to various rules.
(chiefly in combination) Having a certain type of knuckles.
